mainEntity.name: Will a zirconia crown last longer than glass-ceramic under heavy biting forces?

acceptedAnswer.text: Zirconia crowns typically demonstrate greater longevity in high-stress situations due to their superior fracture resistance. However, crown lifespan depends on multiple factors including oral hygiene, bite patterns, and maintenance. Both materials can provide excellent long-term service when appropriately selected for the clinical situation and properly maintained.

mainEntity.name: Can I grind my teeth with either type of crown?

acceptedAnswer.text: Neither crown material should be subjected to deliberate grinding forces, as this can cause premature wear or fracture. Patients with bruxism (teeth grinding) may benefit from zirconia's enhanced strength characteristics, but protective night guards are often recommended regardless of crown material to minimise stress on both natural teeth and restorations.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which crown material is right for my bite force?

acceptedAnswer.text: Crown material selection requires professional assessment of your individual bite patterns, jaw muscle strength, and specific clinical requirements. Your dentist will evaluate factors including tooth position, opposing dentition, and any parafunctional habits to recommend the most appropriate material for your circumstances.

mainEntity.name: Do stronger crown materials affect the opposing teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both glass-ceramic and zirconia can be designed to provide appropriate contact with opposing teeth. Surface treatments and occlusal adjustments help ensure comfortable function whilst minimising excessive wear on natural tooth structure. Regular monitoring allows early detection of any wear patterns that might require attention.

mainEntity.name: Will insurance cover the stronger zirconia option?

acceptedAnswer.text: Insurance coverage varies significantly between providers and individual policies. Many insurance plans provide similar coverage for different crown materials, though some may have specific limitations or requirements. It's advisable to verify coverage details with your insurance provider when discussing treatment options with your dental team.

mainEntity.name: Can either crown type break from normal eating?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both glass-ceramic and zirconia crowns are designed to withstand normal chewing forces when properly fabricated and placed. Fractures from typical eating are uncommon but may occur due to factors such as inadequate crown thickness, underlying tooth problems, or excessive forces. Avoiding hard foods and protecting teeth from trauma help minimise fracture risks.
